ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the circuit shown in figure, with two Zener diodes each with a voltage of 6.3V and a forward voltage of 0.7V, the output voltage \( U_0 \) is ________ V.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of the figure is the input power supply U1=18 V, connected through the upper 1 kΩ resistor to the output node on the right; the positive terminal of U0 on the right is at this output node, and the negative terminal is at the bottom common rail. From the output node downward there is a parallel voltage-regulating branch, containing two voltage-regulator diodes connected in reverse series, and below them a power supply labeled 2 V is further connected in series to the lower reference rail. Then reason: according to the data given in the problem, the voltage-regulating value of each voltage-regulator tube is 6.3 V, and the forward conduction voltage drop is 0.7 V. When this back-to-back voltage-regulator diode group is clamping, one undergoes reverse breakdown and the other conducts forward, and the total voltage drop is 6.3 V + 0.7 V = 7.0 V. There is also a 2 V power supply below it, so the output voltage is U0 = 2 V + 7.0 V = 9.0 V. Also, the input 18 V through 1 kΩ is higher than the clamping voltage, so the branch can conduct and clamp.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit: identify the output node after the 1 kΩ resistor, the bottom rail as the negative reference for U0, and the vertical shunt branch consisting of two back-to-back Zener diodes above a 2 V source. Then use the text-given diode data: in this polarity the back-to-back Zener pair drops one Zener voltage plus one forward voltage, 6.3 V + 0.7 V = 7.0 V. Add the 2 V reference shown below the diodes to get U0 = 2 V + 7.0 V = 9 V. Optionally check that the 18 V supply through 1 kΩ is higher than 9 V, so the clamp conducts.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct clamp-voltage route: it uses the visual series stack from the output node to the 2 V reference and sums the voltage drops of the conducting Zener pair plus the offset source. This is the natural single-solution path for this circuit.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read from the figure that an 18 V source feeds the output node through a 1 kΩ resistor; U0 is measured from that output node to the bottom rail. From the output node down to the bottom rail there is a shunt branch containing two oppositely oriented Zener diodes in series and then a 2 V source/reference at the bottom.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the stated values: each Zener has breakdown voltage 6.3 V and forward voltage 0.7 V; the question asks for numeric U0 in volts.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For two oppositely connected Zener diodes in a conducting clamp, one diode operates in Zener breakdown at 6.3 V and the other is forward biased at 0.7 V, so the diode stack drop is 6.3 + 0.7 = 7.0 V. The 2 V source raises the lower end of the diode stack above the bottom rail, so the output clamp level is 2 + 7 = 9 V. The 1 kΩ resistor only limits current; with 18 V input it can supply current, confirming the clamp is active.
